question: Does base attention gain at the verified reader heads supply the cross-cue response dose missing from every writer-only compiler?
novelty: Writer coefficient orientation and rank-one reader axes transfer, but dose does not. No prior predictor uses the selected readers' own base attention strength onto the subject positions.

frozen_design.fit_test: same original A1+A2 balanced fit and exact fresh capable A1/A2/P test populations as the writer-only falsifier
frozen_design.writer_feature: scale-invariant summed writer coefficient s = projection / writer-vector norm
frozen_design.reader_gain_features: block9 target: [s, s*m9h1, s*m9h4, 1]; block11 target: [s, s*m11h3, 1], where m is base attention probability summed over the two subject positions at final query
frozen_design.baseline: writer-only [s,1] map for each reader fitted on the identical joint A1+A2 rows
frozen_design.axes: shared original-corpus rank-one reader axes fitted jointly across A1+A2

predictions.pred_a_authority_capability_closure: all authority, capability, alignment, and capture closures pass
predictions.pred_b_reader_gain_predicts_coefficients: both target coefficient correlations absolute r>=0.70 on fresh A1/A2
predictions.pred_c_reader_gain_program_material: target program retains >=0.65 full response and is donorward on >=0.75 fresh A1/A2 rows
predictions.pred_d_reader_gain_beats_writer_only: target A2 causal fraction exceeds same-run writer-only by >=0.15 and reaches >=0.60
predictions.pred_f_price_exact: 45 forwards, 1161 examples, 295 records, 11 scalars, 512 axes, zero backwards/updates

terminal_rules.invalid: authority, rows, capability, closure, coverage, finiteness, or price fails
terminal_rules.base_gain_insufficient: valid reader-gain model does not repair dose; next object must include writer-induced key/value change rather than base attention mass

interpretation_limits: Base attention mass is a reader-local causal-interface variable, not a learned task label.
A pass remains bounded to the two cue lexicons and frames.
Failure closes static base-gain predictors and redirects to exact attention response terms.
